canvas.$description: Usage redefined (2026-08-08) to "canvas and playground container" — narrower than the prior "page/app background" meaning, now specifically the live-preview/demo container surface. Value moved off neutral.black (was briefly byte-identical to bg.surface) to gray.700, one step lighter than the reverted bg.surface (gray.800) — an intentional inversion of the usual dark-mode elevation cue (raised content is normally lighter than the canvas behind it), confirmed at explicit direction given canvas's narrower Storybook-specific usage. Known accessibility gap, accepted for now and slated for an upcoming text-color pass rather than blocking this background change: text.secondary on this value measures 4.00:1 (fails the 4.5:1 AA text floor) and text.tertiary measures 2.96:1 (fails even the 3:1 non-text floor); text.primary is fine at 6.59:1. Don't place text.secondary/tertiary literal text directly on bg.canvas until that follow-up lands.

overlay.$description: Dimming scrim behind Dialog/Drawer/overlays (Backdrop atom). No text sits directly on it, so it isn't a WCAG contrast pairing — opacity is applied separately, compositionally, via the opacity.* scale rather than baked into this token, matching how color and opacity stay separate token categories everywhere else. Shared across all 4 themes since dimming what's behind isn't a brand-dependent decision. Reordered (2026-08-20) to sit right after bg.canvas, per explicit direction — no value change.

skeleton.$description: New token (2026-08-16), added for Skeleton alongside the light-mode fix (see that theme's own description for the full rationale) — dark mode's existing gray.900 value (vs bg.surface/gray.800 = 1.40:1) was already visibly correct, confirmed live in Storybook, so this is a rename onto a dedicated token, not a value change. Light mode was revised same day to a brand-tinted purple.200/emerald.200; dark mode deliberately stays neutral gray rather than following suit, mirroring bg.brand-subtle's own established precedent (that token drops its brand tint entirely in dark mode too — purple.950 was tried and rejected there for failing text.link/icon.brand contrast and colliding with bg.canvas, see that token's own description). bg.skeleton hosts no text, so the contrast reason doesn't directly transfer, but the same underlying tension likely does: a dark, low-chroma brand tint reads as almost the same as plain gray at this end of the lightness curve, so there's no real visual payoff for the added complexity of a fourth brand-specific value. Revisit if a specific dark brand-tinted value is ever requested. Reordered (2026-08-20) to sit right after bg.overlay, per explicit direction — no value change.

surface.$description: Reverted (2026-08-08) from neutral.black back to gray.800, paired with bg.canvas moving off neutral.black in the same edit — surface and canvas are no longer byte-identical; canvas (gray.700) now reads slightly lighter than surface (gray.800), see bg.canvas's own description for why. Reintroduces a border.default/bg.surface collision (both gray.800, 1.00:1) that the neutral.black value had incidentally fixed — reverted docs.css's table-border/section-divider rule back to border.neutral-subtle (gray.900, 1.40:1 against this value) to compensate. Contrast re-verified: text.primary 9.66:1, text.secondary 5.86:1, text.tertiary 4.34:1 — all still clear AA. Usage redefined in the same edit to "page, card, sheet and drawer background". bg.surface-raised (a separate token for "an elevated surface, paired with a shadow") was retired (2026-08-20) — it was byte-identical to this token (both gray.800), so keeping two names for one value added a lookup with no payoff. Every former bg.surface-raised consumer now uses this token directly.

brand.$description: Dark value moved emerald.500 → emerald.300 (2026-08-21, at explicit direction) — same fix already shipped for bg.neutral (Phase 34) and bg.danger/warning/success/info (2026-08-20 consolidation): a lighter dark-mode fill paired with dark text, instead of a mid-tone fill paired with white/near-white text. emerald.300 vs bg.surface (gray.800) = 6.07:1 (fill/dot distinguishability, was 4.63:1 on the old emerald.500). Also absorbs the retired bg.brand-indicator (2026-08-21) — that token existed as a lighter step than bg.brand specifically because bg.brand's own old dark value didn't clear 3:1 well enough for a standalone dot (4.63:1); the new emerald.300 clears it more comfortably than the old indicator token itself did, so the separate token is no longer needed — every consumer (Badge's dot mode) now uses this token directly.

brand-hover.$description: Hover state of bg.brand. Dark value changed to emerald.200 (2026-08-21, at explicit direction) — one step lighter than the new bg.brand dark value, matching the X.300→X.200 dark-mode hover direction every other consolidated tone already uses (bg.danger red.300→red.200, bg.neutral gray.300→gray.200, etc.). text.on-brand (gray.900) on emerald.200 = 10.55:1, clears 4.5:1 with a wide margin. Also resolves a pre-existing inconsistency: purple-dark's hover used to go darker (purple.500→purple.600) while emerald-dark's went lighter (emerald.500→emerald.400) — both brands now use the same lighten-in-dark-mode direction.

brand-subtle.$description: Moved from emerald.950 to gray.900 (2026-08-09) at explicit direction, mirroring the same change on purple-dark (see that file's own description for the full rationale: gray.700 was tried and rejected first for failing text.link/icon.brand contrast and colliding with bg.canvas). text.link (emerald.400) on gray.900 measures 6.49:1, still comfortably clear of the 4.5:1 AA text floor. Drops the emerald tint from this token entirely in dark mode, same trade-off as purple's — accepted collision with bg.subtle (also gray.900) in exchange for staying distinct from bg.canvas and clearing AA.

brand-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — one step lighter than brand-subtle (gray.900), matching this system's standard dark-mode hover direction, same as purple-dark.json's own bg.brand-subtle-hover. text.link (emerald.400) on gray.800 = 4.63:1, passes AA (the tightest of the 12 new hover pairings verified for this change, still clear of the 4.5:1 floor).

danger.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from red.500 to red.300, one step lighter. Old value measured only 2.90:1 against dark bg.surface, an outright WCAG 1.4.11 failure for a small standalone graphic (this is what bg.danger-indicator, now retired, existed to work around). red.300 vs bg.surface (dark) = 5.67:1. text.on-danger moves to red.900 alongside this change (8.22:1 against this new value) — see that token's own description. See purple-light.json's own bg.danger description for the full shared-value rationale (bg/text/border/icon.danger now all resolve to this same step per mode).

danger-hover.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from red.400 to red.200, alongside bg.danger's own dark move (red.500 → red.300) to preserve the same relative hover-lightening gap. text.on-danger (red.900 as of this change) on red.200 = 10.68:1.

danger-subtle.$description: Moved from red.900 to red.950 (2026-07-27), one step darker — the mirror-opposite move to the light theme's red.100 → red.50, preserving the same relative gap from each theme's pole. text.danger (red.300) on red.950 = 10.32:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 8.22:1 on red.900). Not part of the 2026-08-20 danger token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated dark tint.

danger-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses danger-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (red.900), one step lighter, matching this system's standard dark-mode hover direction. text.danger (red.300) on red.900 = 8.22:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching danger-subtle's own brand-independence. Not part of the 2026-08-20 danger token consolidation.

warning.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from amber.500 to amber.300, two steps lighter. Old value measured 3.05:1 against dark bg.surface — technically cleared WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 non-text floor but with almost no margin (this is what bg.warning-indicator, now retired, existed to widen). amber.300 vs bg.surface (dark) = 5.80:1. text.on-warning moves to amber.900 alongside this change (8.19:1 against this new value) — see that token's own description. See purple-light.json's own bg.warning description for the full shared-value rationale (bg/text/border/icon.warning now all resolve to this same step per mode).

warning-hover.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from amber.400 to amber.200, alongside bg.warning's own dark move (amber.500 → amber.300) to preserve the same relative hover-lightening gap. text.on-warning (amber.900 as of this change) on amber.200 = 10.54:1.

warning-subtle.$description: Moved from amber.900 to amber.950 (2026-07-27), one step darker — the mirror-opposite move to the light theme's amber.100 → amber.50, preserving the same relative gap from each theme's pole. text.warning (amber.300) on amber.950 = 10.44:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 8.19:1 on amber.900). Not part of the 2026-08-20 warning token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated dark tint.

warning-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses warning-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (amber.900), one step lighter, matching this system's standard dark-mode hover direction. text.warning (amber.300) on amber.900 = 8.19:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching warning-subtle's own brand-independence. Not part of the 2026-08-20 warning token consolidation.

success.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from green.500 to green.300, two steps lighter. Old value measured 3.28:1 against dark bg.surface — a real pass, but thinner than desired for a dedicated indicator use (this is what bg.success-indicator, now retired, existed to widen). green.300 vs bg.surface (dark) = 6.01:1. text.on-success moves to green.900 alongside this change (8.19:1 against this new value) — see that token's own description. See purple-light.json's own bg.success description for the full shared-value rationale (bg/text/border/icon.success now all resolve to this same step per mode).

success-hover.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from green.400 to green.200, alongside bg.success's own dark move (green.500 → green.300) to preserve the same relative hover-lightening gap. text.on-success (green.900 as of this change) on green.200 = 10.32:1.

success-subtle.$description: Moved from green.900 to green.950 (2026-07-27), one step darker — the mirror-opposite move to the light theme's green.100 → green.50, preserving the same relative gap from each theme's pole. text.success (green.300) on green.950 = 10.68:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 8.19:1 on green.900). Not part of the 2026-08-20 success token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated dark tint.

success-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses success-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (green.900), one step lighter, matching this system's standard dark-mode hover direction. text.success (green.300) on green.900 = 8.19:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching success-subtle's own brand-independence. Not part of the 2026-08-20 success token consolidation.

info.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from blue.500 to blue.300, two steps lighter. Old value measured 3.09:1 against dark bg.surface — a real pass, but thinner than desired for a dedicated indicator use (this is what bg.info-indicator, now retired, existed to widen). blue.300 vs bg.surface (dark) = 5.85:1. text.on-info moves to blue.900 alongside this change (8.20:1 against this new value) — see that token's own description. See purple-light.json's own bg.info description for the full shared-value rationale (bg/text/border/icon.info now all resolve to this same step per mode).

info-hover.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from blue.400 to blue.200, alongside bg.info's own dark move (blue.500 → blue.300) to preserve the same relative hover-lightening gap. text.on-info (blue.900 as of this change) on blue.200 = 10.46:1.

info-subtle.$description: Moved from blue.900 to blue.950 (2026-07-27), one step darker — the mirror-opposite move to the light theme's blue.100 → blue.50 (2026-07-27), preserving the same relative gap from each theme's pole. text.info (blue.300) on blue.950 = 10.51:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 8.20:1 on blue.900). Not part of the 2026-08-20 info token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated dark tint. Dark mode has no equivalent to light mode's razor-edge margin (see purple-light.json's own bg.info-subtle description) — text.info's dark value was already blue.300 before and after, so nothing changed here.

info-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses info-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (blue.900), one step lighter, matching this system's standard dark-mode hover direction. text.info (blue.300) on blue.900 = 8.20:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching info-subtle's own brand-independence. Not part of the 2026-08-20 info token consolidation.

neutral.$description: Merged with the retired bg.neutral (gray.500, offline/dot-only fill) and renamed from bg.neutral-strong (2026-08-21). Dark value moved gray.600 → gray.300 (step 2, 2026-08-21, at explicit direction) — gray.600 alone couldn't satisfy both real uses in dark mode (2.14:1 as a dot against bg.surface, failing 3:1). Fixed the same way bg.danger/warning/success/info were already fixed in the 2026-08-20 consolidation: switch to a lighter dark-mode fill paired with dark (not white) text, rather than try to keep one gray working for both a light-on-dark dot and a dark-on-light text fill. gray.300 vs bg.surface (gray.800) = 5.86:1 (dot use, clears 3:1 with a wide margin, better than the original bg.neutral's own 3.10:1); text.on-neutral's own dark value moved white → gray.900 in the same pass (see that token's own description), giving gray.900-on-gray.300 = 8.21:1 (text use, clears 4.5:1 with a wide margin). Real, visible change for Badge.solidNeutral/Tag.solidNeutral/Tag.selected.outlineNeutral/Tooltip in dark mode — dark text instead of white, not just a number — confirmed live before considering this done.

neutral-hover.$description: Renamed from bg.neutral-strong-hover (2026-08-21), hover state of bg.neutral (formerly bg.neutral-strong). Dark value moved gray.700 → gray.200 (step 2, 2026-08-21, at explicit direction) — same fix as bg.neutral's own dark value (see that token's description): one step lighter than the new gray.300 base, matching the X.300→X.200 dark-mode hover direction every other tone's own solid fill already uses (e.g. bg.danger red.300→red.200). gray.200 vs bg.surface (gray.800) = 7.47:1; text.on-neutral's new dark value (gray.900) on gray.200 = 10.47:1 — both comfortably clear their floors.

neutral-subtle.$description: Renamed from bg.subtle (2026-08-20), grouped with the other neutral tokens here instead of sitting up near bg.canvas/bg.surface — no value change. Usage redefined (2026-08-08) to "hover fill for tertiary/ghost controls, dashboard panel, neutral accent", value moved from gray.800 to gray.900 in the same edit — also resolved a since-removed collision with the also-since-removed bg.surface-raised (formerly also gray.800), since gray.900 was a step further from that value than gray.800 was from itself. Contrast re-verified: text.secondary-on-this-token (Tag/Badge subtleNeutral) 8.21:1 (was 4.00:1 on the gray.700 this token's history below rejected, and comfortably clear of gray.800's own value too), text.primary 13.53:1 — both clear AA. Byte-identical to border.neutral-subtle (also gray.900) — nothing currently pairs the two, flagged here as a heads-up. History: was byte-identical to bg.surface-raised on gray.800 (2026-07-27 review) — a hover fill invisible against the elevated card it sits on; gray.700 was tried and rejected then for failing the text.secondary pairing at 4.00:1, which is why gray.900 (not gray.700) is the value used to break that collision.

neutral-subtle-hover.$description: Renamed from bg.subtle-hover (2026-08-20), grouped with the other neutral tokens here — no value change. Originally added 2026-08-17, found adding Tag's whole-tag clickable/selectable mode — bg.neutral-subtle's own hover step, one primitive scale step lighter (the dark-mode hover direction bg.brand-subtle-hover/etc. already use). Byte-identical to bg.surface (also gray.800, since bg.surface-raised was retired into bg.surface — see that token's own description) — a harmless collision, since nothing pairs the two directly. text.secondary (Tag/Badge subtleNeutral's own paired text) on gray.800 = 7.47:1, comfortably passes AA.

track.$description: New token (2026-08-22), added for ProgressBar's empty/unfilled track — was reusing bg.neutral-subtle, the same 'existing token reused for an unverified new purpose' bug that led to bg.skeleton (Phase 18). Dark value carried over unchanged from bg.neutral-subtle (gray.900, 1.40:1 vs bg.surface) — still fails the 3:1 non-text floor WCAG 1.4.11 asks for graphical objects required to understand content, accepted at explicit user direction for the same reason as the light-mode value (see purple-light.json/emerald-light.json for the full rationale) — a deliberate, informed exception, not a verified pass. Brand-agnostic. Revisit with gray.400 (4.34:1) if this needs to actually clear 3:1 later.

code.$description: Dark value moved from blue.950 to gray.700 (2026-08-09) at explicit direction — code pill drops the blue tint in dark mode specifically, moving to a neutral gray fill instead. Light mode is unchanged (blue.50). Byte-identical to border.code's own dark value (also gray.700, see that token) — the pill's border is effectively invisible against its own fill in dark mode, an explicit flat/borderless treatment for this mode, not an oversight. text.secondary on this value measures 5.10:1, clear of the 4.5:1 AA text floor. Retired 2026-08-20 in favor of bg.info-subtle directly (which reintroduced a blue tint in dark mode, since bg.info-subtle's own dark value is blue.950, not this token's gray.700 — see the guideline log's own note on that reversal); restored the same day, reversing that retirement — every former consumer uses this token, and its flat gray.700 dark treatment, again.

secondary.$description: Moved from gray.300 to gray.200 (2026-08-08) at explicit direction, driven by bg.canvas's move to gray.700 the same day: text.secondary on bg.canvas measured 4.00:1 on gray.300 (fails the 4.5:1 AA text floor), gray.200 clears it at 5.10:1. Also improves against every other bg.* pairing: 7.47:1 on bg.surface (was 5.86:1 on gray.300), 10.47:1 on bg.subtle (was 8.21:1).

tertiary.$description: Moved from gray.400 to gray.300 (2026-08-08) at explicit direction, same motivation as text.secondary's move above. Still doesn't fully clear the 4.5:1 text floor against bg.canvas (gray.300 on gray.700 measures 4.00:1) — it does clear the 3:1 non-text floor there, but this token's own literal-text uses (Text color="tertiary", Divider label, Input placeholder) need 4.5:1, same standard that ruled out gray.500 originally (see history below). No primitive step between 300 and 400 exists to close that last gap without also moving past text.secondary's own gray.200. Given that, `bg.canvas` should never host `text.tertiary` literal text — enforced by guideline note (see guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md) rather than by chasing a lighter value here, since 5.86:1 on bg.surface and 8.21:1 on bg.subtle (this token's actual intended surfaces) are both comfortably clear at gray.300. History: gray.500 originally failed AA (needs 4.5:1) for this token's literal-text uses; gray.400 gave 6.08:1 against the surfaces it was verified on at the time (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen).

on-brand.$description: Text/icons on a solid bg.brand fill. Dark value changed to gray.900 (2026-08-21, at explicit direction), replacing a per-brand split that had accumulated rather than been designed: purple-dark used white, emerald-dark used gray.950 (emerald.500 was too light for white text) — now both brand themes share one value, matching bg.brand's own dark value becoming brand-agnostic in relative terms (each brand's own tone.300 step). gray.900 on the new bg.brand dark = 8.51:1; on bg.brand-hover dark = 10.55:1 — both clear 4.5:1 with a wide margin, well past the old purple pairing's own 4.51:1 near-miss (white on purple.500).

on-danger.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from gray.950 to red.900, so a solid bg.danger fill in dark mode reads as a monochromatic red surface (fill + text both red-family) rather than red fill + neutral-gray text. red.900 on bg.danger's own new dark value (red.300) = 8.22:1, more margin than the previous gray.950 pairing (5.22:1). Light themes keep white — see purple-light.json / emerald-light.json's own description.

on-info.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from gray.950 to blue.900, so a solid bg.info fill in dark mode reads as a monochromatic blue surface (fill + text both blue-family) rather than blue fill + neutral-gray text. blue.900 on bg.info's own new dark value (blue.300) = 8.20:1, more margin than the previous gray.950 pairing (5.56:1). Light themes keep white — see purple-light.json / emerald-light.json's own description.

on-success.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from gray.950 to green.900, so a solid bg.success fill in dark mode reads as a monochromatic green surface (fill + text both green-family) rather than green fill + neutral-gray text. green.900 on bg.success's own new dark value (green.300) = 8.19:1, more margin than the previous gray.950 pairing (5.91:1). Light themes keep white — see purple-light.json / emerald-light.json's own description.

on-warning.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from gray.950 to amber.900, so a solid bg.warning fill in dark mode reads as a monochromatic amber surface (fill + text both amber-family) rather than amber fill + neutral-gray text. amber.900 on bg.warning's own new dark value (amber.300) = 8.19:1, more margin than the previous gray.950 pairing (5.49:1). Light themes keep white — see purple-light.json / emerald-light.json's own description.

on-neutral.$description: Text on a solid bg.neutral fill (Badge solid variant). Dark value moved white → gray.900 (step 2, 2026-08-21, at explicit direction) — bg.neutral's own dark value moved gray.600 → gray.300 in the same pass (see that token's description) to fix a real 3:1 non-text-contrast failure on the dot use case; white text on the new lighter gray.300 would only measure 1.72:1, so dark mode switches to dark text instead, the same pattern text.on-danger/warning/success/info already use in dark mode (e.g. text.on-danger = red.900, not white). gray.900 on gray.300 = 8.21:1, clears 4.5:1 with a wide margin.

link.$description: Token update (2026-08-20), at explicit direction — moved off the brand anchor (was emerald.400 in this theme, purple.300 in the other) to a shared blue.300, now literally identical across both brand themes and both modes. De-brands link color entirely — see purple-light.json's own text.link description for the full rationale, including the two real consumers (Avatar's default fill, Storybook's own toolbar) moved to text.brand to preserve their previous appearance. blue.300 vs bg.surface (gray.800) = 5.85:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 4.63:1 on the old emerald.400 — an improvement, and this theme's own tightest text.link margin before this change). Byte-identical to text.info's own dark value as a direct consequence.

brand.$description: Accent text drawn from the brand color (2026-07-27) — for emphasis/labels, not links. Originally reused text.link's own resolved value; text.link was de-branded to a shared blue (2026-08-20, see that token's own description), so this token now stands on its own — value unchanged, still emerald.400. emerald.600 (the literal brand anchor) on bg.surface (gray.800) is only 2.42:1, failing AA — emerald.400 gives 4.63:1, freshly re-verified (2026-08-20); an earlier recorded figure of 3.39:1 here had been computed against a stale gray.900 value predating Phase 9's bg.surface revert and was never corrected until now.

danger.$description: Unchanged by the 2026-08-20 danger token consolidation (already red.300) — now also the shared value bg.danger, border.danger, and icon.danger resolve to in dark mode. See purple-light.json's own text.danger description for the consolidation this is part of.

warning.$description: Unchanged by the 2026-08-20 warning token consolidation (already amber.300) — now also the shared value bg.warning, border.warning, and icon.warning resolve to in dark mode. See purple-light.json's own text.warning description for the consolidation this is part of.

success.$description: Unchanged by the 2026-08-20 success token consolidation (already green.300) — now also the shared value bg.success, border.success, and icon.success resolve to in dark mode. See purple-light.json's own text.success description for the consolidation this is part of.

info.$description: Unchanged by the 2026-08-20 info token consolidation (already blue.300) — now also the shared value bg.info, border.info, and icon.info resolve to in dark mode. See purple-light.json's own text.info description for the consolidation this is part of.

default.$description: Moved from gray.800 to gray.950 (2026-08-08) at explicit direction. Fixes the exact-collision with bg.surface (also gray.800, 1.00:1) noted in Phase 9 of guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md — this pairing now measures 1.80:1. Also improves against bg.canvas (1.46:1 → 2.64:1). Trade-off: gets slightly worse against bg.subtle (1.40:1 → 1.28:1). Neither the old nor the new value clears the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 non-text floor against any of these real component-hosting surfaces (Input/Textarea/Button/Kbd/Divider/IconButton all use this token) — a pre-existing gap this change doesn't create, confirmed and accepted rather than assumed.

neutral-subtle.$description: Renamed from border.subtle (2026-08-21), same border.* rotation as the light file (see border.neutral-subtle's own light-mode description for the full four-way mapping). Dark counterpart, value unchanged (gray.900).

neutral.$description: Renamed from border.strong (2026-08-21), same border.* rotation (see the light-mode border.neutral's own description). Dark counterpart, value unchanged (gray.600) — the default resting border on Checkbox/Blockquote/Kbd, hover-state border on Select/Input/Textarea/Button's secondary variant/IconButton/Indicators, same as light.

neutral-strong.$description: Renamed from border.neutral (2026-08-21), part of the border.* rotation (see border.neutral-subtle's own description). Dark counterpart to border.neutral-strong (light) — see that token's own description for its purpose (and why it isn't the one Tag's outline variant actually consumes). Doesn't reuse the token now named border.neutral's own dark value (gray.600, only 2.14:1 against dark bg.surface — well under 3:1) for the same reason the light value doesn't. gray.400 vs bg.surface (dark) = 4.34:1, a comfortable margin.

strong.$description: Renamed from border.neutral-strong (2026-08-21), part of the border.* rotation (see border.neutral-subtle's own description). Dark counterpart to border.strong (light) — found adding Tag's selectable solid-variant ring. Reuses the same primitive step text.secondary already uses in dark mode (gray.200), independently tracked. gray.200 vs bg.surface (dark) = 7.47:1. Now consumed directly by Tag's outline/selected-solid-neutral rings (Tag.module.css).

brand.$description: Dark value changed emerald.400 → emerald.300 (2026-08-21, at explicit direction), matching bg.brand's own dark value now that both are the same tone.300 step — previously border.brand reused border.focus's dark value instead of bg.brand's own (see Phase 22), since bg.brand's old dark step measured only 2.24:1/3.41:1 against dark bg.surface, too weak for a real border. That workaround is no longer needed: emerald.300 vs bg.surface (gray.800) = 6.07:1, up from 4.63:1 on the old emerald.400 — a real improvement, not just a rename.

brand-subtle.$description: Renamed from border.brand (2026-08-20), for naming consistency with its sibling family tokens (border.danger-subtle/warning-subtle/success-subtle/info-subtle all carry the -subtle suffix for the same decorative-only role; this one hadn't, despite being the exact same kind of token). Value unchanged. Brand-accent border, decorative-only (2026-07-27, revised from emerald.400). Dark value moved off the literal emerald.100 shared with light mode to emerald.900 (2026-08-16, mirroring the same change on purple-dark — see that file's own description) — emerald.100 on bg.brand-subtle (gray.900) measured 12.46:1, a stark high-contrast ring that read nothing like light mode's own low-key accent. emerald.900 on gray.900 is 1.08:1, mirroring light mode's own 1.09:1 (emerald.100 on emerald.50) — both intentionally subtle. This token is for decorative UI accents, not a border that identifies a component/state boundary, so WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 floor doesn't apply here (border.focus/border.danger remain contrast-verified since those ARE state-identifying).

danger.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from red.400 to red.300, absorbing border.danger-strong's former role (that token is retired — every former consumer now uses this token directly) and matching bg.danger/text.danger/icon.danger's shared dark step. red.300 vs bg.surface (dark) = 5.67:1, an improvement over the previous 4.13:1. See purple-light.json's own border.danger description for the consolidation this is part of.

danger-subtle.$description: Family-matched decorative-accent border, dark counterpart to border.danger-subtle (light) — follows the same emerald.900-in-dark-mode pattern established for border.brand-subtle above. Not neutralized to a shared gray the way border.brand-subtle's dark value is: family accents keep their own tint in dark mode (bg.danger-subtle here is red.950, not gray.900 — see that token's own description). Pairs with bg.danger-subtle for any component's danger-tinted ring, not limited to one specific component — first used by Avatar's `colorful` danger variant (2026-08-16), but not scoped to it. red.900 on red.950 is 1.26:1, comparably subtle to border.brand-subtle's own 1.08:1 dark pairing. Brand-agnostic — identical value in every brand theme. Not part of the 2026-08-20 danger token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated decorative step.

See purple-light.json's own border.warning description for the consolidation this is part of.

Brand-agnostic. Not part of the 2026-08-20 warning token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated decorative step.

code.$description: Dark value moved from blue.900 to gray.700 (2026-08-09) at explicit direction, matching bg.code's own move to gray.700 in dark mode — the two are byte-identical there, an explicit flat/borderless pill treatment for dark mode specifically (light mode keeps the blue.100/blue.50 pairing and its visible border, unchanged). Briefly paired with bg.info-subtle instead (2026-08-20, when bg.code was retired) and measured 2.63:1 against that fill; bg.code was restored the same day, reversing that retirement, so this token is back to its original byte-identical-with-bg.code dark treatment. Original description: paired with bg.code (2026-08-08) — blue.100/blue.900, a purely decorative border, not one that identifies a component/state boundary, so WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 floor doesn't apply — same accepted class as border.brand-subtle.

brand.$description: Moved from emerald.400 to emerald.300 (2026-08-09) at explicit direction, mirroring the same change on purple-dark (see that file's own description for the full rationale: emerald.400 passed the 3:1 non-text floor against bg.surface but failed against bg.canvas). emerald.300 measures 6.07:1 on bg.surface, 4.15:1 on bg.canvas — both comfortably clear, the latter also clearing the stricter 4.5:1 text floor for headroom.

on-brand.$description: New token (2026-08-22), completing the icon and icon.on- pattern for brand — dark counterpart to icon.on-brand (light); see that token's own description. gray.900 on bg.brand's own dark value (purple.300/emerald.300) = 7.45:1/8.51:1.
